topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and sets out the learning objectives concerning cancer treatments.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover traditional treatment modalities including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy alongside their mechanisms, systemic toxicities, and resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic vulnerabilities and genetic defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain therapeutic strategies designed to target specific vulnerabilities of cancer cells, such as hormone dependency, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors, resistance mechanisms, and drug addiction
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how oncogenically hyperactivated kinases are targeted by small-molecule inhibitors and detail the emergence of resistance mutations, bypass pathways, and drug addiction.

topics.label: Antibody-based targeted therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the mechanisms and applications of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates directed against tumor surface antigens.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell-directed strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the evidence for cancer immune surveillance and detail immunotherapeutic approaches that harness T cells through checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific engagers, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Therapeutic challenges, historical trends, and future directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the ongoing challenges of tumor heterogeneity and resistance, historical trends in survival, and emerging directions and ethical considerations in cancer management.
